fixes.what: The publish job has no guard for the case where the agent writes neither output file. Step 'The agent stopped' is gated on hashFiles('stop.json') != '' , but the four steps that follow — 'Number the revision', 'Validate the revised work order', 'Refuse a work order that touches forbidden paths' and 'Post it and route' — are gated only on steps.stop.outputs.stopped != 'true'. That condition is true both when the agent legitimately stopped AND when it returned no output whatsoever, and grep finds no hashFiles('work-order.json') guard anywhere in the file. So when the agent writes nothing, bump-version.mjs:22 reads a nonexistent file and the job dies with a bare ENOENT naming version bookkeeping, which is both a misleading diagnosis for triage and the reason the download step's own stated intent — continue-on-error: true, 'validation says so by name' — can never be reached: bump-version runs before validate and fails the job first. The same unguarded shape almost certainly repeats in the other agent-output workflows (sdlc-plan.yml, sdlc-review.yml, sdlc-qa.yml), which fetch their artifacts and then run scripts over the result.
fixes.fix: Add a hashFiles('work-order.json') != '' guard to the four steps in the publish job of sdlc-root-cause.yml, mirroring the existing stop.json idiom at line 403: 'Number the revision', 'Validate the revised work order', 'Refuse a work order that touches forbidden paths' and 'Post it and route' should each run only if steps.stop.outputs.stopped != 'true' AND hashFiles('work-order.json') != ''. Then insert one explicit step between the copy loop and those four that fails the job when neither work-order.json nor stop.json exists, emitting '::error::root-cause wrote neither work-order.json nor stop.json — no revision to publish' together with the agent-transcript.mjs metadata already printed just above it, so the run names the real cause instead of a missing-file crash three steps later. Apply the same guard shape to the publish jobs of sdlc-plan.yml, sdlc-review.yml and sdlc-qa.yml, which have the same copy-then-consume structure.
fixes.diagnosis: The root-cause agent produced no output at all, and the red step is three steps downstream of that. It ran 110 turns for 27 minutes and $5.59 and wrote neither work-order.json nor stop.json — its only two Write calls went to /tmp/probe/t14.mjs and /tmp/probe/sweep.mjs, scratch files outside the repository that the upload path (work-order.json, stop.json, root-cause-transcript.json) never picks up, which is why the root-cause-output artifact is 421 bytes and holds only the transcript. The agent still reported success: the result line reads subtype success, is_error false, num_turns 110, and the diagnose job exited green. The failure surfaced in publish at step 'Number the revision', where bump-version.mjs:22 does readFileSync on a work-order.json that was never written and dies with a bare ENOENT — a missing-input crash that names a file nobody was supposed to produce, so the log points at version bookkeeping rather than at the agent that returned nothing. The framework cannot currently tell those two cases apart: sdlc-root-cause.yml guards the stop branch with hashFiles('stop.json') != '' but guards bump-version, validate, check-forbidden and post-work-order only on steps.stop.outputs.stopped != 'true', which is equally true when the agent wrote nothing, and there is no hashFiles('work-order.json') guard anywhere in the file. That also defeats the workflow's own stated intent at the download step — continue-on-error: true with the comment 'validation says so by name' — because bump-version runs before validation and kills the job first, so the validation that was meant to name the failure never runs. This is not transient and not a plan defect: nothing timed out, no rate or quota limit was hit, the provider returned success, and prior_signatures is empty with occurrences 1, so this exact signature is new — but the pattern of an agent spending 27 minutes and returning nothing is not something a retry fixes by itself, and I cannot explain why the agent abandoned the task after 110 turns from this log: it records 104 Bash calls and two /tmp probes but not the reason it stopped short. Escalating for a person rather than rerunning on a guess. The expensive work did NOT survive and resume would be a lie — the probe scripts went to /tmp on a runner that no longer exists. Prior work is untouched and remains where it was: PR #13 still open at 71e2e89, and previous-work-order.json (version 3, mode committed) as the standing plan.
fixes.evidence: failed-run.log:1154-1156 result {"subtype":"success","is_error":false,"num_turns":110} — the agent called it a success and the diagnose job exited 0; :1448-1451 the transcript summary the publish job printed: 'tools: Bash x104, Read x2, Write x2', 'Write /tmp/probe/t14.mjs (4016 chars)', 'Write /tmp/probe/sweep.mjs (3078 chars)', 'final reply 80 chars' — both Writes are under /tmp, neither is work-order.json, and an 80-char reply holds no plan for --recover to find; :1237 'With the provided path, there will be 1 file uploaded' for a path listing three files, and :1266 'Final size is 421 bytes'; :1459-1462 'sdlc: uncaughtException: ENOENT ... open work-order.json' at .sdlc/bin/bump-version.mjs:22 — the red step; .github/workflows/sdlc-root-cause.yml:416 guards bump-version on 'steps.stop.outputs.stopped != true' while :403 guards the stop branch on "hashFiles('stop.json') != ''", and grep -c "hashFiles('work-order.json')" returns 0, so no step distinguishes 'the agent stopped' from 'the agent produced nothing'; :384 'continue-on-error: true' with the comment 'validation says so by name', unreachable because bump-version precedes validate at :416/:421.
